# Overview

This report calculates the TOPOSCORE for each VE800-001 metagenomic sample and
summarizes it over time by cohort and overall response. The TOPOSCORE is a gut
microbiota score that the source paper linked to immune checkpoint therapy
(ICT) outcome.

Source paper:
Derosa L, Iebba V, Silva C ...
Custom scoring based on ecological topology of gut microbiota associated with
cancer immunotherapy outcome
Cell, 187, 3373-3389.e16
https://www.cell.com/cell/fulltext/S0092-8674(24)00538-5

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(readxl)
library(here)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(emmeans)
library(downloadthis)

if (!dir.exists(here("toposcore_analysis", "output"))) dir.create(here("toposcore_analysis", "output"), recursive = TRUE)

# Saves a figure to toposcore_analysis/output/ and returns a download button for it. Call this
# before printing the plot so the button renders above the figure.
figure_download_button <- function(plot, filename, width, height) {
  path <- here("toposcore_analysis", "output", filename)
  ggsave(path, plot, width = width, height = height, dpi = 300)
  download_file(
    path = path,
    output_name = tools::file_path_sans_ext(filename),
    button_label = "Download figure (PNG)",
    button_type = "default",
    has_icon = TRUE,
    icon = "fa fa-save"
  )
}

response_palette <- c(
  "#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a", "#eda100",
  "#e87ba4", "#008300", "#4a3aa7", "#e34948"
)
```

# Load data

## Toposcore species relative abundance

Toposcore species (from the paper's supplemental table,
`mmc2_toposcore_species.xlsx`) were matched to the MetaPhlAn species in Excel
before import. The workbook has three sheets: exact matches, possible matches
(names that likely changed between MetaPhlAn database versions), and unmatched
species. `SIG` gives each species' signature (SIG1 or SIG2) from the paper.

Sample columns are pivoted to long format, and the MGS sample ID is taken from
each report filename.

```{r import-metaphlan}

metaphlan_path <- here(
  "toposcore_analysis", "input", "VE800_metaphlan_metaphlan-db_combined_reports.xlsx"
)

id_cols <- c(
  "clade_name", "Query name", "Source row", "Name in this file",
  "Match type", "CLUSTER", "SIG", "Reason"
)

species_matches <- read_excel(metaphlan_path, sheet = "species matches") |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = !any_of(id_cols),
    names_to = "filename",
    values_to = "relative_abundance"
  ) |>
  rename(
    Species.toposcore = "Query name",
    Species.mpa4 = "Name in this file"
  ) |> 
  rename_with(\(x) make.names(x, unique = TRUE)) |> 
  rename("Cluster" = "CLUSTER")

possible_matches <- read_excel(metaphlan_path, sheet = "possible matches") |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = !any_of(id_cols),
    names_to = "filename",
    values_to = "relative_abundance"
  ) |>
  rename(
    Species.toposcore = "Query name",
    Species.mpa4 = "Name in this file"
  ) |> 
  mutate("Match type" = "Partial match") |> 
  rename_with(\(x) make.names(x, unique = TRUE)) |> 
  rename("Cluster" = "CLUSTER")

toposcore_species <- species_matches |>
  bind_rows(possible_matches) |>
  mutate(MGS.Sample.ID = str_split_i(filename, "_", 1) |> str_sub(1, -3))

no_match <- read_excel(metaphlan_path, sheet = "unmatched species") |> 
  rename(Species.toposcore = "Query name") |> 
  mutate("Match type" = "No match", Species.mpa4 = NA) |> 
  rename_with(\(x) make.names(x, unique = TRUE))

species_distinct <- toposcore_species |> 
  select(Species.toposcore, Species.mpa4, SIG, Match.type) |> 
  distinct() |> 
  bind_rows(no_match)

```

## Clinical metadata {.tabset}

Clinical metadata (`2026-10-07_VE800_metadata_for_paper.csv`) is joined to the
species data by MGS sample ID. `"NA"` strings are converted to missing values.

Done in the metadata file before import:

- Off-treatment (Off TX) patients are set to `Overall_Response` = `PD`.
- Patients with `Overall_Response` = `NE` or `NE Restart` are not included.

Excluded samples:

- MetaPhlAn files with no match in the metadata (no visit assignment).
- Samples with a missing visit name.
- End-of-treatment (EOT) samples, which are not pre-specified timepoints.

Timepoints: all summaries, plots, and models use `Visit.Name.Norm`
("Timepoint" in figures and tables), which converts each cycle-day visit to
its study day:

| Visit.Name | Visit.Name.Norm (Timepoint) |
|---|---|
| Screen | Screen |
| Baseline | Baseline |
| C1D1 | D1 |
| C1D3 | D3 |
| C1D7 | D7 |
| C1D14 | D14 |
| C1D21 | D21 |
| C2D1 | D30 |
| C3D1 | D58 |
| C4D1 | D86 |
| C5D1 | D114 |
| C6D1 | D142 |
| C7D1 | D170 |
| C8D1 | D198 |
| C10D1 | D254 |

```{r import-clinical}
mgs_metadata <- read_csv(
  here("toposcore_analysis", "input", "2026-10-07_VE800_metadata_for_paper.csv")
)

# inner_join drops MetaPhlAn files with no matching sample in the metadata
toposcore_species_clinical <- toposcore_species |>
  inner_join(mgs_metadata, by = "MGS.Sample.ID") |>
  arrange(Subject_ID, Timepoint, SIG, Species.toposcore) |>
  mutate(
    Overall_Response = if_else(
      Overall_Response == "NA", NA, Overall_Response
    )
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Visit.Name = if_else(
      Visit.Name == "NA", NA, Visit.Name
    )
  ) |> 
  filter(Visit.Name != "EOT") # EOT samples are not included in the analysis because they are not pre-specified timepoints and are not available for all subjects.

# Set visit order for plotting and tables
visit_name_levels <- c(
  "Screen", "Baseline", "C1D1", "C1D3", "C1D7", "C1D14", "C1D21",
  "C2D1", "C3D1", "C4D1", "C5D1", "C6D1", "C7D1", "C8D1", "C10D1", "EOT"
)
visit_name_norm_levels <- c(
  "Screen", "Baseline", "D1", "D3", "D7", "D14", "D21", "D30",
  "D58", "D86", "D114", "D142", "D170", "D198", "D254", "EOT"
)

# factor() silently turns values missing from the levels into NA
unlisted_visits <- c(
  setdiff(toposcore_species_clinical$Visit.Name, visit_name_levels),
  setdiff(toposcore_species_clinical$Visit.Name.Norm, visit_name_norm_levels)
)
if (length(unlisted_visits) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Visits missing from the factor levels: ",
    paste(unique(unlisted_visits), collapse = ", ")
  )
}

toposcore_species_clinical <- toposcore_species_clinical |>
  mutate(
    Visit.Name = factor(Visit.Name, levels = visit_name_levels),
    Visit.Name.Norm = factor(Visit.Name.Norm, levels = visit_name_norm_levels)
  )

# Count the final number of metagenome files included in the analysis
num_metagenome_files <- toposcore_species_clinical |>
  group_by(Cohort, Overall_Response) |>
  distinct(filename) |>
  summarize(N_files = n())

num_subjects <- toposcore_species_clinical |>
  group_by(Cohort, Overall_Response) |>
  distinct(Subject_ID) |>
  summarize(N_subjects = n())
```

# TOPOSCORE calculation

From the paper:

> S score computed as the difference of proportions between present (relative
> abundance > 0) SIG2 and SIG1 MGS and scaled from 0 to 1:
> S = (#SIG2/45 - #SIG1/37 + 1)/2. A score of 0 indicates that all MGS of the
> SIG1 signature have strictly positive relative abundances and all MGS of the
> SIG2 signature have null relative abundances. Conversely, a score of 1
> indicates that all MGS of the SIG1 signature have null relative abundances and
> all MGS of the SIG2 signature have strictly positive relative abundances.

- SIG1: 37 species associated with poor ICT response
- SIG2: 45 species associated with good ICT response

The TOPOSCORE also counts Akkermansia (`Akkermansia SGB 9226`) in every
sample, including when absent:

- **Normal** (> 0% to 4.799%): SIG2
- **High** (> 4.799%): SIG1
- **Absent** (0%): SIG1

All other species count only when present (relative abundance > 0). Because
Akkermansia adds one species to either signature, both denominators increase
by one:

TOPOSCORE = (#SIG2/46 - #SIG1/38 + 1)/2

From the paper:

> Normal levels of Akk (0 < Akk % 4.799%, Akknorm) may be considered as a surrogate of host fitness in comparison with abnormal levels (Akk R 4.8%, Akkhigh) or the absence of Akk (Akk0). Starting from here, gray zone patients who harbored physiological Akk levels (about 19% of the whole cohort) were incorporated into the SIG2 category (to create the ‘‘SIG2+’’ group), while gray zone patients devoid of (Akk0)or harboring supraphysiologically high Akk levels (23% and 4% of the whole cohort, respectively) were incorporated into the SIG1 category (to create the ‘‘SIG1+’’ group).

```{r calc-toposcores}
calc_toposcores <- toposcore_species_clinical |>
  mutate(
    is_akk = Species.toposcore == "Akkermansia SGB 9226",
    SIG_plus = case_when(
      is_akk & relative_abundance > 0 & relative_abundance <= 4.799 ~ "SIG2",
      is_akk & relative_abundance > 4.799 ~ "SIG1",
      is_akk & relative_abundance == 0 ~ "SIG1",
      TRUE ~ SIG
    ),
    # Other species count only when present; absent Akkermansia counts as SIG1
    counted = relative_abundance > 0 | (is_akk & relative_abundance == 0)
  ) |>
  group_by(
    Subject_ID, Timepoint, Visit.Name, Visit.Name.Norm, MGS.Sample.ID,
    Cohort, Response_Wk8, Response_Wk16, Response_Wk24, Response_Wk32,
    Response_Wk40, Overall_Response
  ) |>
  summarise(
    SIG1_count = sum(SIG_plus == "SIG1" & counted),
    SIG2_count = sum(SIG_plus == "SIG2" & counted),
    # Denominators include Akkermansia, which can count toward either signature
    TOPOSCORE = (SIG2_count / 46 - SIG1_count / 38 + 1) / 2,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(Subject_ID, Visit.Name.Norm)
```

```{r toposcore-summary-table}
toposcore_summary <- calc_toposcores |>
  group_by(Cohort, Visit.Name.Norm) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean = mean(TOPOSCORE, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(TOPOSCORE, na.rm = TRUE),

toposcore_summary |>

  kable(caption = "TOPOSCORE by cohort and timepoint")
```

# LME model of TOPOSCORE over time {.tabset}

A linear mixed effects model is fit separately for each cohort to test for
change from Baseline:

`TOPOSCORE ~ Visit.Name.Norm + (1 | Subject_ID)`

- Timepoint is categorical, with Baseline as the reference.
- A random intercept per subject handles repeated samples. Cohorts are too
  small for random slopes.
- Timepoints with fewer than 3 subjects in a cohort are dropped.
- Each timepoint is compared with Baseline using emmeans (Satterthwaite df).
  P-values and CIs use `adjust = "dunnettx"`, a close approximation of
  Dunnett's adjustment, within each cohort (not across cohorts).
- Subjects without a Baseline sample still contribute through their other
  timepoints.

**Statistical outcome** (Dunnett-adjusted)

- TOPOSCORE changes over time in all three cohorts (timepoint F-test
  p < 0.001 in CRC, Gastric, and Melanoma).
- Screen and Baseline do not differ in any cohort (−0.010 to +0.007, all
  p > 0.99), so pre-treatment scores are stable.
- In every cohort, TOPOSCORE **decreases** after treatment starts (a less
  favorable SIG1/SIG2 balance).
- **Melanoma** (20 subjects): significant decrease at every timepoint from D1
  through D170 (about −0.09 to −0.18; p ≤ 0.01), with no return to Baseline.
- **Gastric** (20 subjects): significant decrease from D1 through D30 (about
  −0.13 to −0.17; p < 0.001). D58 is not significant (−0.086, p = 0.19).
- **CRC** (14 subjects): smaller decrease, significant from D3 through D30
  (about −0.07 to −0.11; p ≤ 0.02). D1 is borderline (−0.066, p = 0.06).
  From D58 on, no timepoint differs from Baseline (all p > 0.4), suggesting
  partial recovery.
- All CRC and Gastric subjects are PD, so overall response is examined only
  in Melanoma.

```{r lme-fit}
min_subjects <- 3

lme_data <- calc_toposcores |>
  filter(!is.na(Cohort)) |>
  group_by(Cohort, Visit.Name.Norm) |>
  filter(n_distinct(Subject_ID) >= min_subjects) |>
  ungroup()

fit_cohort_lme <- function(df) {
  if (!"Baseline" %in% df$Visit.Name.Norm) {
    stop("No Baseline timepoint with >= ", min_subjects, " subjects in a cohort")
  }
  df <- df |>
    mutate(Visit.Name.Norm = fct_relevel(fct_drop(Visit.Name.Norm), "Baseline"))
  lmer(TOPOSCORE ~ Visit.Name.Norm + (1 | Subject_ID), data = df, REML = TRUE)
}

# Baseline is releveled to first, so ref = 1 is Baseline
baseline_contrasts <- function(model) {
  emmeans(model, ~ Visit.Name.Norm, lmer.df = "satterthwaite") |>
    contrast(method = "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = 1, adjust = "dunnettx") |>
    summary(infer = TRUE) |>
    as_tibble()
}

lme_fits <- lme_data |>
  nest(.by = Cohort) |>
  mutate(
    model = map(data, fit_cohort_lme),
    singular = map_lgl(model, isSingular),
    n_subjects = map_int(data, \(d) n_distinct(d$Subject_ID)),
    n_samples = map_int(data, nrow),
    visit_anova = map(model, \(m) as_tibble(anova(m))),
    contrasts = map(model, baseline_contrasts)
  )

lme_contrasts <- lme_fits |>
  select(Cohort, contrasts) |>
  unnest(contrasts) |>
  mutate(
    Visit.Name.Norm = factor(
      str_remove(contrast, " - Baseline"),
      levels = visit_name_norm_levels
    ),
    significant = p.value < 0.05
  ) |>
  arrange(Cohort, Visit.Name.Norm)
```

## Overall timepoint effect

Type III F-test of timepoint within each cohort. A significant result means
TOPOSCORE differs across timepoints; the contrasts show where. A singular fit
means the subject-level variance was estimated as zero.

```{r lme-anova}
lme_fits |>
  select(Cohort, n_subjects, n_samples, singular, visit_anova) |>
  unnest(visit_anova) |>
  select(
    Cohort, n_subjects, n_samples, singular,
    num_df = NumDF, den_df = DenDF, F_value = `F value`, p_value = `Pr(>F)`
  ) |>
  mutate(across(c(den_df, F_value), \(x) round(x, 2)), p_value = signif(p_value, 3)) |>
  kable(caption = "Overall effect of timepoint on S score, by cohort")
```

## Contrasts vs Baseline

Estimated TOPOSCORE at each timepoint minus Baseline, with Dunnett-adjusted
95% CI and p-value.

```{r lme-contrasts}
lme_contrasts |>
  select(Cohort, contrast, estimate, SE, df, lower.CL, upper.CL, p.value) |>
  mutate(
    across(c(estimate, SE, lower.CL, upper.CL), \(x) round(x, 3)),
    df = round(df, 1),
    p.value = signif(p.value, 3)
  ) |>
  kable(caption = "TOPOSCORE change from Baseline by timepoint (LME, Dunnett-adjusted)")
```

# LME model of Melanoma TOPOSCORE with overall response {.tabset}

For Melanoma only, a timepoint × overall response interaction model is fit, so
each response group has its own trajectory:

`TOPOSCORE ~ Visit.Name.Norm * Overall_Response + (1 | Subject_ID)`

- Subjects with a missing `Overall_Response` are excluded.
- A timepoint is kept only if every response group has at least
  `r min_subjects` subjects there. The first tab shows the resulting counts.
- The most common response group is the reference.
- Three sets of comparisons:
  - **Change from Baseline by response:** Dunnett-adjusted within each group.
  - **Response difference by timepoint:** unadjusted.
  - **Difference in change from Baseline** (interaction contrast):
    Dunnett-adjusted across timepoints.

Group sizes are small; treat estimates from cells with few subjects as
descriptive.

**Statistical outcome** (12 PD and 8 SD subjects, Baseline through D58)

- The timepoint × response interaction is significant (F = 3.87, p < 0.001):
  PD and SD follow different trajectories.
- The response main effect is not significant (F = 1.06, p = 0.32), but this
  average over timepoints hides the timepoint-dependent difference.
- **SD starts higher:** SD is above PD at Baseline (+0.10, p = 0.002) and D1
  (+0.11, p < 0.001). From D3 on, the groups do not differ (all p > 0.2).
- **Both groups decrease from Baseline:**
  - PD: about −0.10 to −0.13 from D1 through D30 (all p < 0.001). D58 is not
    significant (−0.074, p = 0.28; only 3 PD subjects).
  - SD: −0.088 at D1 (p = 0.03), then about −0.20 to −0.24 from D3 through
    D58 (all p < 0.001).
- **SD decreases more:** the difference is significant at D21 (−0.12,
  p = 0.04), D30 (−0.14, p = 0.006), and D58 (−0.15, p = 0.01), but not from
  D1 through D14.
- In short, SD subjects start with a higher TOPOSCORE but lose that advantage
  by D3.

```{r melanoma-lme-fit}
melanoma_data <- calc_toposcores |>
  filter(Cohort == "Melanoma", !is.na(Overall_Response)) |>
  mutate(Overall_Response = fct_drop(factor(Overall_Response)))

# Keep visits where every response group has enough subjects
melanoma_kept_visits <- melanoma_data |>
  distinct(Visit.Name.Norm, Overall_Response, Subject_ID) |>
  count(Visit.Name.Norm, Overall_Response) |>
  complete(Visit.Name.Norm, Overall_Response, fill = list(n = 0)) |>
  group_by(Visit.Name.Norm) |>
  filter(all(n >= min_subjects)) |>
  distinct(Visit.Name.Norm) |>
  pull(Visit.Name.Norm)

if (!"Baseline" %in% melanoma_kept_visits) {
  stop(
    "Baseline does not have >= ", min_subjects,
    " subjects in every Melanoma response group"
  )
}

melanoma_data <- melanoma_data |>
  filter(Visit.Name.Norm %in% melanoma_kept_visits) |>
  mutate(
    Visit.Name.Norm = fct_relevel(fct_drop(Visit.Name.Norm), "Baseline"),
    # Most frequent response becomes the reference level
    Overall_Response = fct_infreq(Overall_Response)
  )

melanoma_model <- lmer(
  TOPOSCORE ~ Visit.Name.Norm * Overall_Response + (1 | Subject_ID),
  data = melanoma_data, REML = TRUE
)

melanoma_emm_grid <- emmeans(
  melanoma_model, ~ Visit.Name.Norm * Overall_Response,
  lmer.df = "satterthwaite"
)

contrast_table <- function(x) {
  summary(x, infer = TRUE) |> as_tibble()
}

melanoma_visit_contrasts <- melanoma_emm_grid |>
  contrast(
    method = "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = 1, by = "Overall_Response",
    adjust = "dunnettx"
  ) |>
  contrast_table()

melanoma_response_contrasts <- melanoma_emm_grid |>
  contrast(method = "revpairwise", by = "Visit.Name.Norm", adjust = "none") |>
  contrast_table()

# Columns 1:2 hold the visit and response contrast labels
melanoma_interaction_contrasts <- melanoma_emm_grid |>
  contrast(interaction = c("trt.vs.ctrl", "revpairwise"), adjust = "dunnettx") |>
  contrast_table() |>
  unite("contrast", 1:2, sep = ", ")

melanoma_emm <- as_tibble(melanoma_emm_grid) |>
  mutate(Visit.Name.Norm = factor(Visit.Name.Norm, levels = visit_name_norm_levels))
```

## Subjects by response and timepoint

```{r melanoma-lme-counts}
melanoma_data |>
  distinct(Overall_Response, Visit.Name.Norm, Subject_ID) |>
  count(Overall_Response, Visit.Name.Norm) |>
  mutate(Visit.Name.Norm = factor(Visit.Name.Norm, levels = visit_name_norm_levels)) |>
  arrange(Visit.Name.Norm) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Visit.Name.Norm, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  left_join(
    count(distinct(melanoma_data, Overall_Response, Subject_ID),
          Overall_Response, name = "Total subjects"),
    by = "Overall_Response"
  ) |>
  kable(caption = "Melanoma subjects per overall response and timepoint (timepoints used in the model)")
```

## Model tests

Type III F-tests for timepoint, overall response, and their interaction. A
significant interaction means trajectories differ between response groups; if
so, the main effects are not interpreted on their own.

```{r melanoma-lme-anova}
as_tibble(anova(melanoma_model), rownames = "term") |>
  select(
    term, num_df = NumDF, den_df = DenDF,
    F_value = `F value`, p_value = `Pr(>F)`
  ) |>
  mutate(
    across(c(den_df, F_value), \(x) round(x, 2)),
    p_value = signif(p_value, 3),
    singular_fit = isSingular(melanoma_model)
  ) |>
  kable(caption = "Melanoma: timepoint × overall response effects on TOPOSCORE")
```

## Change from Baseline by response

Estimated change from Baseline within each response group (Dunnett-adjusted
within group).

```{r melanoma-lme-visits}
format_contrasts <- function(tbl, ...) {
  tbl |>
    select(..., contrast, estimate, SE, df, lower.CL, upper.CL, p.value) |>
    mutate(
      across(c(estimate, SE, lower.CL, upper.CL), \(x) round(x, 3)),
      df = round(df, 1),
      p.value = signif(p.value, 3)
    )
}

melanoma_visit_contrasts |>
  format_contrasts(Overall_Response) |>
  kable(
    caption = "Melanoma: TOPOSCORE change from Baseline by response (Dunnett-adjusted)"
  )
```

## Response difference by timepoint

Estimated difference between response groups at each timepoint (unadjusted).

```{r melanoma-lme-response}
melanoma_response_contrasts |>
  format_contrasts(Visit.Name.Norm) |>
  kable(caption = "Melanoma: TOPOSCORE difference between response groups by timepoint")
```

## Difference in change from Baseline

Difference between response groups in change from Baseline. For example,
"D7 - Baseline, SD - PD" is SD's change to D7 minus PD's change
(Dunnett-adjusted across timepoints).

```{r melanoma-lme-interaction}
melanoma_interaction_contrasts |>
  format_contrasts() |>
  kable(
    caption = "Melanoma: difference between response groups in change from Baseline"
  )
```

## LME contrast plot - Melanoma

Lines are model-estimated means with 95% CIs; points are observed TOPOSCOREs.

```{r melanoma-lme-plot, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5}
melanoma_lme_plot <- ggplot(
  melanoma_emm,
  aes(Visit.Name.Norm, emmean, color = Overall_Response, group = Overall_Response)
) +
  geom_point(
    data = mutate(
      melanoma_data,
      Visit.Name.Norm = factor(Visit.Name.Norm, levels = visit_name_norm_levels)
    ),
    aes(y = TOPOSCORE),
    alpha = 0.35, size = 1.5,
    position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.1, dodge.width = 0.5)
  ) +
  geom_line(position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_pointrange(
    aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), size = 0.4
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = response_palette) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(
    x = "Timepoint",
    y = "TOPOSCORE",
    color = "Overall response",
    title = "Melanoma: model-estimated TOPOSCORE by timepoint and overall response",
    subtitle = "LME timepoint × response interaction model; estimated means with 95% CI"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "top"
  )

figure_download_button(
  melanoma_lme_plot, "lme_melanoma_toposcore_by_response.png",
  width = 9, height = 5
)

melanoma_lme_plot
```

# Export

Per-sample TOPOSCOREs, the summary table, and the model contrasts are written
to `toposcore_analysis/output/`. Figures are saved there as each plot is drawn.

```{r export}
write_csv(calc_toposcores,here("toposcore_analysis", "output", "toposcores.csv"))
write_csv(toposcore_summary, here("toposcore_analysis", "output", "toposcore_summary.csv"))
write_csv(
  select(lme_contrasts, -significant),
  here("toposcore_analysis", "output", "lme_toposcore_contrasts_vs_baseline.csv")
)
write_csv(
  bind_rows(
    mutate(
      melanoma_visit_contrasts,
      comparison = "visit vs Baseline within response"
    ),
    mutate(melanoma_response_contrasts, comparison = "response by visit"),
    mutate(
      melanoma_interaction_contrasts,
      comparison = "difference in change from Baseline"
    )
  ),
  here("toposcore_analysis", "output", "lme_melanoma_response_contrasts.csv")
)

```
